sentences.text: Opisthodactylus is an extinct genus of ñandú, a type of rhea, that lived in Miocene Argentina.
This bird belongs to the family Rheidae, which includes modern rheas.
The species O. kirchneri was formally described in 2017 by Noriega and colleagues.
Fossils of O. horacioperezi were discovered in association with fossils of the giant ground sloth Patagorhacos terrificus.
Three species of Opisthodactylus have been described, including the type species O. patagonicus.
The time range for Opisthodactylus spans from the Aquitanian to the Piacenzian, approximately 21 to 3 million years ago.
Fossils of Opisthodactylus date from the Early to Late Miocene epochs.
This extinct bird lived in the Santa Cruz, Chichinales, and Andalhuala Formations of Argentina.
